facts.text: Dillard was founded in 1846 around the homestead of Captain John Dillard, one of the first white settlers in northern Rabun County.
The Tallulah Falls Railroad reached Dillard in 1906, turning the town into a bustling lumber hub where hundreds of rail cars shipped logs each year.
In the same year, 1906, the Georgia General Assembly incorporated the place as the Town of Dillard, formalizing its status.
John Dillard’s grandson built a stagecoach way station on the historic Rabun Turnpike, a north‑south route that once served as a toll road.
Dillard sits in the Little Tennessee River valley, just south of the North Carolina border and surrounded by the Blue Ridge Mountains.
The town’s name honors the Dillard family, whose early settlement and land purchases helped shape the region’s development.
